scope.description: Twenty-two trials on hand-built four-node clusters whose nodes all share the same settings (50ms heartbeat, election and lease), one cluster per trial: twenty adverse trials in which one voter is isolated first and left to campaign while the others still have the leader in view and only then the leader and the nonvoter are isolated, and two plain controls in which no voter campaigns beforehand. Each trial forces leadership onto node 0, demotes node 3 to nonvoter, records a baseline confirmation, and then polls the leader's verifications while watching the two remaining voters for a leader.
assumptions: Pre-vote is enabled by default in this snapshot, so a node that cannot reach a majority stays at its current term; the harness records the campaigner's state and term so the outcome shows whether a pre-existing higher-term candidacy formed at all.
Per-node settings are identical here, so any difference from the mixed-timer runs is history rather than configuration.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses; a competing leader is detected by reading the two isolated nodes' states.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what will be interpreted.
excluded: No application read is served, so the measured quantity is whether a confirmation coexists with a competing leader.
No on-disk store, no network transport and no multi-process execution.
Only the uniform configuration is exercised here; the mixed-timer path is covered by the sibling experiments.

parameters.recorded_operands: adverse, preexisting_candidate, campaigner_state, campaigner_term, leader_term, polls, confirmations, last_confirmation_ms, first_peer_leader_ms, confirmations_after_peer_leader, confirmation_after_peer_leader, leader_stepped_down, leader_applied_index

basis.prefix: Each trial builds four nodes by hand with identical settings, waits for any leader, transfers leadership to node 0 and waits until it reports Leader, demotes node 3 to nonvoter with DemoteVoter and waits, records a baseline confirmation through the verification channel the exported API uses, and applies one command. In the adverse trials it first isolates node 1 from the others in both directions and waits up to three seconds for that node to report Candidate with a term above the leader's, recording whether that happened, before isolating the leader and the nonvoter from both remaining voters; the plain controls go straight to that second isolation. The harness then polls the verification path every 2ms while the leader still reports Leader, records the last confirmation's elapsed time and the first time either remaining voter reports Leader, and emits one summary event per trial with the counts, the campaigner's final state and term, the leader's term, and whether any confirmation followed a competing leader.

comparisons.description: Prediction under test: with a voter already campaigning, at least one confirmation follows a competing leader. Every adverse trial that fails this is a witness that the separation survives the adverse history, which is the outcome the source reading predicts.
Control: with no voter campaigning beforehand and shared settings, no confirmation follows a competing leader.
